_comment: Permission set for the unattended scheduled run. Handed to `claude --settings`, and only
effective together with `--permission-mode manual --permission-prompts none` (see run_daily.ps1).
Tested behaviour on Claude Code 2.1.278 (module 03 test T10, 2026-09-19):
- bare tool rules in `allow` work            e.g. "Write"
- argument patterns work for Bash            e.g. "Bash(git:*)" correctly denies git
- PATH patterns work in `deny`               e.g. "Write(.secrets/**)" correctly blocks
- PATH patterns DO NOT match in `allow`      "Write(outputs/**)" silently denied everything
So protection is expressed as a deny-list, not an allow-list: anything not denied and not
explicitly allowed still needs a prompt, and an unanswerable prompt is a denial. Keep the deny
list in step with any new top-level directory added to this repo.
HOW allow AND deny DIFFER FOR Bash (measured, T10 + T15, 2026-09-19):
Module 01 is agentic and issues COMPOUND commands, e.g.
cd "D:/..." && mkdir -p outputs/... && python fetch_tasks.py > outputs/t.json && python - <<'E' ... E; rm outputs/t.json
- `allow` requires EVERY component to be allowed. So Bash(python:*) does NOT admit the command
above, because `cd`, `mkdir` and `rm` are not allowed - narrowing Bash stopped the pipeline
dead twice. Hence bare `Bash`.
- `deny` fires if ANY component matches. Verified directly: with deny Bash(git:*), the command
`cd . && echo hello && git status --short` was DENIED. So the deny list below IS a real
boundary for Bash, not merely best-effort.
WHY rm IS NOT DENIED: because deny is absolute and cannot carry a path exception, Bash(rm:*) also
blocked module 01's own cleanup of its temp file inside outputs/ - the scheduled run failed on
exactly that (T15). Dropping it is the price of a reliable pipeline; git remains denied, which is
the rule that actually protects the repository and its secrets from an off-script run.
NET EFFECT. Enforced: every non-Bash tool outside `allow` is denied (WebFetch, WebSearch, Task and
anything added later); the Read/Write/Edit deny paths hold for Claude's own file tools; and no shell
command containing git can run. Not enforced: any other shell action, including reading .secrets
from inside a python subprocess. Bare Bash was accepted by the owner on 2026-09-19.
Real containment rests on prompt.txt, the published skills, and this task launching nothing else.
If module 01 is ever made non-agentic (parsing moved into a script), narrow Bash back immediately.
